_source: Rule matching idea adapted from alibaba/open-code-review (Apache-2.0). Rules are this repo's own conventions.

exclude.reason: generated DI; review its inputs instead
sli_common submodule; review in its own repo

checks: Imports only Dart and domain types: no Flutter, data, presentation, core, get_it, injectable, dio or firebase.
Repository interfaces are abstract and return domain entities, never models.
Use cases receive repositories through the constructor and hold no UI state.
Never imports presentation.
Data sources only transport or store; they never navigate, show UI or read BuildContext.
Errors are typed and mapped; secrets and PII are redacted before logging.
Repository implementations are bound with @LazySingleton(as: Interface).
Annotated @injectable and receives use cases through the constructor; no getIt lookups.
State is immutable Equatable with copyWith and carries recoverable errors.
One-shot actions are revisioned typed UiEffect values; no BuildContext, navigation or l10n.
Every await is followed by an isClosed check before emit.
BLoC is used only for documented event or concurrency needs.
Never imports data.
Navigation, dialogs, snackbars and l10n live in listeners, driven by UiEffect.
Uses sli_common public APIs, not direct shadcn_flutter imports.
User-facing text comes from ARB, not string literals.
BlocBuilder scope is narrow (buildWhen or BlocSelector) and long lists use builders.
Scopes follow di-scopes: @injectable for state owners, @lazySingleton for stateless services.
Only composition roots resolve getIt.
Never imports presentation, data or domain.
Network inspectors and verbose logging cannot run in production.
Tokens and PII never reach logs, Alice or crash reports.
Every key exists in every locale with matching placeholders.
Tests prove behavior, including failure and concurrency paths, not implementation details.
No real network or secrets in unit and widget tests; performance scenarios use the test account from the environment only.
Exported components, deep links and URL schemes are intended and protected.
No secrets, signing material or production keys are committed.
Permission declarations match runtime use; minSdk and deployment targets change only on purpose.
New dependencies are justified, maintained and placed under the right section.
Scripts never print secrets and fail loudly.
Docs, skills and agents match the code and commands that actually exist.
Links resolve and conventions do not contradict project-convention.
